howto.name: PrivaTools converts via Pillow
howto.text: TIFF keeps the alpha channel and is read by archival software that has never heard of WebP.

howto.name: Convert and download
howto.text: Run the conversion. TIFF preserves transparency and is accepted by archival and prepress software that has no idea what WebP is.

faq.q: Does WebP to TIFF lose quality?
faq.a: If your WebP is lossy, TIFF can't restore discarded detail; if it's lossless WebP, the TIFF is pixel-identical. Either way TIFF gives you the lossless container that print and archival tools expect.

faq.q: Why not just keep the WebP?
faq.a: Many print, scanner, and legacy desktop applications don't read WebP at all. TIFF is universally supported by those workflows.

The WebP is uploaded to the PrivaTools server and converted with local image libraries, not a third-party API. Response cleanup removes the input and the TIFF from temporary storage after the result is sent.
